observations: The button is icon-only (an `up-arrow` `ct-icon`, always rendered `aria-hidden`) with its accessible name supplied entirely via the `label` prop, passed through as the composed `ct-button`'s `aria-label`. `label` defaults to the real, descriptive "Return focus to the top of the page" — so this passes as shipped, out of the box, unlike a component that leaves the implementer to supply a name from nothing. Only fails if an implementer explicitly overrides `label` to an empty string.

standard: 1.2.3 Audio Description or Media Alternative (Prerecorded) (Level A)

observations: The component is a single button with no structural relationships (no headings, lists, or form associations) to preserve.
Not a form input.
The component conveys no information through color alone — its single fill color is decorative branding, not a coded meaning.

Verified via `verify-component`: the composed button renders `background-color: #00698f` (`--ct-back-to-top-background-color`) against `color: #fafbfb` (`--ct-back-to-top-color`) — both trace to the same `color.interaction.light.*` primitives CivicTheme's own primary-button contrast pairing already relies on, well above the 4.5:1 minimum.
No visible text to resize. The icon renders in a 1em box (`ct-icon`) that is font-size-relative, so it scales normally under text-resize/zoom rather than clipping or overlapping.
A single small fixed-position control; it does not require reflow at 320px CSS width and does not introduce a second scroll dimension.

Documented implementation deviation (see `back-to-top.ts`'s code comment): because the composed `ct-button` ties its primary variant's `border-color` to the same custom property as its `background-color`, this port could not reproduce upstream's distinct, lighter `--ct-back-to-top-border-color` (#fdfdfd) without modifying the shared `ct-button` component — the rendered border is the same solid color as the fill instead. On a page background close in color to `--ct-color-interaction-light-background` (#00698f), the button's edge could fall short of the 3:1 non-text contrast this criterion requires against its immediate surroundings. Verify against the actual page background this component is placed on.
No visible text.

standard: 1.4.13 Content on Hover or Focus (Level AA)
observations: Hover/focus do not reveal any additional content.
Renders as a real `ct-button` (`kind="link"`, an anchor with `role="button"`), reachable and activatable via keyboard like any other composed `ct-button` instance.
A single focusable control; focus moves through it normally in both directions.
The scroll-position-driven show/hide is not moving, blinking, or auto-updating content in the sense this criterion addresses — it's a static visibility toggle keyed to scroll position, not a timer.

standard: 2.3.1 Three Flashes or Below Threshold (Level A)

observations: This is the inverse of a skip link — it returns to the top of the page rather than bypassing a repeated block at the top, so it does not itself satisfy this criterion (a real skip-to-main-content mechanism is still the implementer's responsibility elsewhere on the page).

The button's visual position (bottom-right, via `position: fixed`) is entirely independent of its DOM position, which is what actually determines its place in the tab order. Compliance depends on the implementer placing the `<ct-back-to-top>` element at a DOM position whose resulting tab-order placement makes sense relative to its always-bottom-right visual placement, rather than, e.g., leaving it stranded mid-document.
Ships with a descriptive, non-generic default accessible name ("Return focus to the top of the page"). Only at risk if an implementer overrides `label` with vague text.
A page-level concern this single component cannot fulfill or block on its own.
Same underlying concern as 2.4.4 above, since `label` is this component's only text — clear as shipped, at risk only if overridden with unclear text.

The composed `ct-button` renders a real `:focus-visible` outline using `--ct-color-interaction-light-focus`, the same primitive `--ct-back-to-top-outline-color` resolves to, so the focus ring is visibly present and correctly themed with no override needed.

Because the button is `position: fixed` at the viewport's bottom-right corner (a genuine risk specific to a fixed-position overlay widget like this one, not a boilerplate concern), compliance depends on the implementer ensuring no other page content's focus indicator ends up rendered behind or clipped by it — e.g. a bottom-right-anchored cookie banner, chat widget, or a focused control that scrolls under this fixed element.
Single-point activation (click/tap) only.
Activates on the standard `click` event (an up-event), not on `pointerdown`/`mousedown`, so an accidental press can still be aborted by moving off the target before release.

This criterion applies to controls with a visible text label that the accessible name must also contain. This button is icon-only with no visible text label, so there is nothing for the accessible name to conflict with.

Measured via `verify-component` on the default preview: the composed button (`size="small"` `ct-button`) renders at 84 x 36 CSS pixels, comfortably clearing the 24 x 24 CSS pixel minimum — unlike a generic icon-only button at a smaller size might.
Inherits the page's `lang` attribute; sets no text content of its own beyond the `aria-label`, which is not itself a language-of-page concern.
Focusing the button triggers no navigation or context change by itself — the scroll-and-focus behavior only runs on click/activation.
No input/selection controls.
No form/validation involved.

The composed `ct-button` provides a real role (`role="button"` on its anchor) and, by default, a real accessible name (`label`, defaulting to "Return focus to the top of the page"). Compliance is conditional only on an implementer not overriding `label` to an empty string — same underlying dependency as 1.1.1 above.

The show/hide toggle is a CSS display change with no live-region announcement, matching upstream's own behavior — appearing/disappearing on scroll is not treated as a status message needing an aria-live announcement.
